"""Posterior-predictive critique of a fitted PyMC cognitive model (CriticAL).

Given an incumbent model that has already been fit to the pooled responses, this
module evaluates LLM-proposed *test statistics* — each a Python function
``test_statistic(df) -> float`` over a trial-level dataframe — under a
posterior-predictive check:

1. ``build_critique_frames`` builds the observed ("human") dataframe and
   ``n_replicates`` model dataframes. Each model dataframe is the observed
   dataframe with its response column overwritten by one posterior-predictive
   draw of the response (``FittedModel.sample_synthetic_responses``). Feature
   columns are identical across all frames, so a statistic that conditions on
   stimulus features sees the same design under the model and the data.
2. ``evaluate_test_statistic`` computes the statistic on the observed frame and
   on every replicate, then forms the two-sided empirical p-value

       p = min(1, 2 · min((n_ge + 1)/(n + 1), (n_le + 1)/(n + 1)))

   (the plus-one keeps finite Monte-Carlo samples from yielding an exact zero)
   and a z-score of the observed value against the replicate distribution.

A statistic whose (raw, uncorrected) two-sided p-value is at or below
``significance_alpha`` is a *significant discrepancy*: concrete evidence of how
the incumbent model fails to reproduce the data, which the next round of
candidate models should address. This is exploratory discrepancy screening, not
confirmatory testing — but because several statistics are screened per round, a
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted q-value (``p_value_fdr``) and flag
(``significant_fdr``, ``n_significant_fdr``) are reported *alongside* the raw
ones so the multiplicity is visible rather than ignored.

This is the statistical core only. The critique agent writes the test-statistic
files and the natural-language synthesis; this module computes the evidence.

CLI (run by the critique agent over a directory of test-statistic files)::

    python3 -m src.critique.ppc \\
        --responses      model_loop/responses.csv \\
        --model          bayesian_fair_coin \\
        --models-dir     model_loop/models \\
        --test-stats-dir iter_0/critique/test_stats \\
        --out            iter_0/critique/ppc_results.json \\
        --cache-dir      .mcmc_cache
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import itertools
import json
import math
import re
import signal
import sys
import threading
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

import numpy as np
from pyprojroot import here

# Ensure repo root on path so "import src..." works when run as a module/script.
# Must precede the src imports below, hence here() rather than the canonical
# src.runtime.config.REPO_ROOT (which resolves the root the same way).
_repo_root = str(here())
if _repo_root not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _repo_root)

from src.models.mcmc_defaults import (  # noqa: E402  (needs sys.path above)
    PRODUCTION_CHAINS,
    PRODUCTION_DRAWS,
    PRODUCTION_TUNE,
)

# Time limits for agent-authored test statistics, which run in the harness
# process (outside the critique agent's own subprocess timeout). A statistic is
# called once on the observed data and once per posterior-predictive replicate
# (1000 in the loop), so a limit on the whole batch — 30 s for 1001 calls, as it
# used to be — is ~30 ms per call, which an ordinary pandas statistic misses on
# experiment 3's 7,680 rows (a groupby/map took ~32 ms per call, a row-wise
# apply ~127 ms), and the critique silently lost its statistics exactly when
# the data were richest. Now:
# - each call has its own wall-clock limit (a hung statistic stops there;
#   ``_time_limit``), and
# - all of one statistic's calls share a budget, so the check of a slow but
#   finite statistic cannot take hours. The budget allows ~0.3 s per call over
#   1001 calls, more than twice the row-wise apply above. The pre-check
#   (``check_test_statistic``) projects one call's time over every call and
#   sets aside a statistic that would exceed it, with that reason, before the
#   check runs.
_TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC = 5.0
_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC = 300.0


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Data structures
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


@dataclass
class TestStatistic:
    """One LLM-proposed test statistic: a ``test_statistic(df) -> float`` function."""

    __test__ = False  # not a pytest test class despite the "Test" prefix

    name: str
    code: str
    description: str = ""


@dataclass
class TestStatisticResult:
    """The outcome of evaluating one test statistic under the PPC.

    ``p_value`` is the two-sided empirical p-value (raw, uncorrected);
    ``p_value_one_sided`` is the upper-tail value (how often the model meets or
    exceeds the observed). ``error`` is non-None when the statistic's code raised
    or returned a non-finite value, in which case the p-values are NaN.
    """

    __test__ = False  # not a pytest test class despite the "Test" prefix

    test_statistic: TestStatistic
    t_observed: float
    t_null: List[float]
    p_value: float
    p_value_one_sided: float = float("nan")
    z_score: float = float("nan")
    p_value_is_floor: bool = False
    error: Optional[str] = None


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Test-statistic loading and execution
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^#\s*name:\s*(.+?)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)
_DESC_RE = re.compile(r"^#\s*description:\s*(.+?)\s*$", re.MULTILINE)


def load_test_statistic_file(path: Path) -> TestStatistic:
    """Load a ``test_statistic(df)`` from a ``.py`` file.

    The file must define a callable named ``test_statistic``. The optional
    ``# name:`` / ``# description:`` header comments (the format the critique
    agent writes) populate the metadata; ``name`` defaults to the file stem.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    code = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "def test_statistic" not in code:
        raise ValueError(f"{path} must define a function named 'test_statistic(df)'")
    name_match = _NAME_RE.search(code)
    desc_match = _DESC_RE.search(code)
    name = name_match.group(1).strip() if name_match else path.stem
    description = desc_match.group(1).strip() if desc_match else ""
    return TestStatistic(name=name, code=code, description=description)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _time_limit(seconds: Optional[float]):
    """Best-effort wall-clock limit for agent-authored code.

    Uses ``SIGALRM``, which only fires on the main thread of a Unix process; in
    any other context (a worker thread, Windows) this is a no-op and the code
    runs unbounded. That is acceptable as a guard: the in-process PPC harness
    runs on the main thread, which is exactly where a hung statistic would
    otherwise stall the whole inner loop.
    """
    if (
        not seconds
        or seconds <= 0
        or not hasattr(signal, "SIGALRM")
        or threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread()
    ):
        yield
        return

    def _handler(signum, frame):
        raise TimeoutError(f"test statistic exceeded {seconds:g}s")

    old = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _handler)
    signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, seconds)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old)


def _compile_test_statistic(code: str) -> Callable[[Any], Any]:
    """Compile test-statistic ``code`` once and return its ``test_statistic`` fn.

    The code runs with ``np``, ``pd``, ``math`` and ``json`` in scope (the same
    surface the critique agent is told it may use). Compiling once (rather than
    re-``exec``-ing per replicate) is faster and means any module-level side
    effects in the agent's code run exactly once.
    """
    import pandas as pd  # local import: pandas is only needed at evaluation time

    namespace: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "np": np,
        "pd": pd,
        "math": math,
        "json": json,
        "__builtins__": __builtins__,
    }
    exec(code, namespace)  # noqa: S102 — executing agent-authored statistic code
    fn = namespace.get("test_statistic")
    if not callable(fn):
        raise ValueError("code must define a callable named 'test_statistic'")
    return fn


def check_test_statistic(
    path: Path, observed_df: Any, *, n_replicates: int = 0
) -> Optional[str]:
    """Run a statistic file once on the observed data, as the check will.

    Returns the error (a raise, a timeout, a non-finite value, or a call slow
    enough that the check's ``1 + n_replicates`` calls would exceed the
    statistic's time budget), or ``None`` when the statistic gives a finite
    number in time. The critique runs this on every statistic before the
    posterior-predictive check, so a broken statistic is reported back to the
    critique agent instead of silently yielding NaN.
    """
    try:
        statistic = load_test_statistic_file(path)
        fn = _compile_test_statistic(statistic.code)
        started = time.monotonic()
        with _time_limit(_TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC):
            value = float(fn(observed_df.copy()))
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
    except Exception as exc:  # an agent-authored statistic that does not run
        return f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        return f"non-finite value on the observed data ({value})"
    projected = elapsed * (1 + n_replicates)
    if projected > _TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC:
        return (
            f"too slow: one call took {elapsed:.2f} s on the {len(observed_df)} "
            f"observed rows, and the check calls it {1 + n_replicates} times "
            f"(~{projected:.0f} s) — over the {_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC:g} s budget per "
            "statistic. Vectorise it (no row-wise apply or Python loops over rows)."
        )
    return None


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Posterior-predictive evaluation
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


class _StatisticCallFailed(Exception):
    """One call of a statistic failed; the message names the error and the call."""


def evaluate_test_statistic(
    test_statistic: TestStatistic,
    human_df: Any,
    model_dfs: List[Any],
) -> TestStatisticResult:
    """Evaluate one statistic on the observed data and the PPC replicates.

    Returns a :class:`TestStatisticResult` with the observed value, the null
    distribution over replicates, the two-sided empirical p-value, and a z-score.
    A statistic whose code raises, which is non-finite anywhere, or which runs
    out of time — a call over ``_TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC`` or all its calls
    over ``_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC`` — returns a result with ``error`` set (saying
    which call) and NaN p-values.
    """
    # Lazily: ``model_dfs`` may build each replicate on demand (the RSA domain's
    # replicates of ~50k trials would not all fit in memory at once).
    n_frames = 1 + len(model_dfs)
    frames = itertools.chain(
        [("the observed data", human_df)],
        ((f"replicate {i + 1} of {len(model_dfs)}", df) for i, df in enumerate(model_dfs)),
    )
    values: List[float] = []
    try:
        fn = _compile_test_statistic(test_statistic.code)
        started = time.monotonic()
        for label, df in frames:
            try:
                with _time_limit(_TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC):
                    values.append(float(fn(df.copy())))
            except Exception as exc:  # say which call failed
                raise _StatisticCallFailed(
                    f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc} (on {label})"
                ) from exc
            spent = time.monotonic() - started
            if spent > _TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC and len(values) < n_frames:
                raise TimeoutError(
                    f"its calls exceeded the {_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC:g} s budget per "
                    f"statistic after {len(values)} of {n_frames} "
                    f"(~{spent / len(values):.2f} s per call)"
                )
    except Exception as exc:  # an agent-authored statistic that does not run
        return TestStatisticResult(
            test_statistic=test_statistic,
            t_observed=float("nan"),
            t_null=[],
            p_value=float("nan"),
            error=str(exc)
            if isinstance(exc, _StatisticCallFailed)
            else f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
        )
    t_obs, t_null = values[0], values[1:]

    t_null_arr = np.asarray(t_null, dtype=float)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(t_null_arr)) or not math.isfinite(t_obs):
        return TestStatisticResult(
            test_statistic=test_statistic,
            t_observed=t_obs,
            t_null=list(t_null_arr),
            p_value=float("nan"),
            error="non-finite test statistic value",
        )

    n = len(t_null_arr)
    n_ge = int(np.sum(t_null_arr >= t_obs))
    n_le = int(np.sum(t_null_arr <= t_obs))
    # Plus-one correction: finite Monte-Carlo samples never give an exact zero
    # p-value, and this defines the floor when the observed value falls outside
    # every replicate.
    p_one = (n_ge + 1) / (n + 1)
    p_two = min(1.0, 2.0 * min((n_ge + 1) / (n + 1), (n_le + 1) / (n + 1)))

    null_mean = float(t_null_arr.mean())
    null_std = float(t_null_arr.std())
    if null_std > 0.0:
        z_score = (t_obs - null_mean) / null_std
    elif t_obs == null_mean:
        z_score = 0.0
    else:
        # Degenerate (deterministic) reference: any discrepancy is infinitely far.
        z_score = math.inf if t_obs > null_mean else -math.inf

    return TestStatisticResult(
        test_statistic=test_statistic,
        t_observed=t_obs,
        t_null=list(t_null_arr),
        p_value=p_two,
        p_value_one_sided=p_one,
        z_score=z_score,
        p_value_is_floor=min(n_ge, n_le) == 0,
    )


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Frame building (PyMC posterior-predictive replicates)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


def build_critique_frames(
    fitted: Any,
    responses_path: Path,
    *,
    n_replicates: int,
    seed: int = 42,
) -> Tuple[Any, List[Any]]:
    """Build the observed frame and the posterior-predictive replicate frames.

    ``fitted`` is a :class:`src.models.pymc_inference.FittedModel`. The observed
    frame is the full responses CSV. Each replicate frame is a copy whose
    observed-response column is overwritten with one posterior-predictive draw
    of the response, so a test statistic conditions on the *same* feature columns
    under the model and the data and only the responses differ.

    ``n_replicates`` is capped at the fitted posterior's draw count (chains ×
    draws); a smaller pool is used with a printed note rather than an error.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    from src.models.data_binding import make_stim_data
    from src.models.model_loading import observed_response_data

    responses_path = Path(responses_path)
    human_df = pd.read_csv(responses_path)
    if human_df.empty:
        raise ValueError(f"No response rows in {responses_path}")

    response_col = observed_response_data(fitted.model)
    if response_col not in human_df.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Response column {response_col!r} (the model's observed pm.Data) is not "
            f"in {responses_path}; columns: {list(human_df.columns)}"
        )

    rows = human_df.to_dict("records")
    stim_data = make_stim_data(fitted.model, rows)

    capacity = _posterior_capacity(fitted)
    n_use = n_replicates
    if capacity is not None and n_replicates > capacity:
        print(
            f"  [critique] requested {n_replicates} PPC replicates but the posterior "
            f"only holds {capacity} draws; using {capacity}",
            flush=True,
        )
        n_use = capacity

    synthetic = fitted.sample_synthetic_responses(
        stim_data, n_datasets=n_use, seed=seed
    )
    synthetic = np.asarray(synthetic)
    if synthetic.shape[1] != len(human_df):
        raise ValueError(
            f"PPC returned {synthetic.shape[1]} responses per replicate but the data "
            f"has {len(human_df)} trials"
        )

    model_dfs: List[Any] = []
    for i in range(synthetic.shape[0]):
        rep = human_df.copy()
        rep[response_col] = synthetic[i]
        model_dfs.append(rep)
    return human_df, model_dfs


def _posterior_capacity(fitted: Any) -> Optional[int]:
    """Number of posterior draws available for PPC (chains × draws), or None.

    Returns None when the fit carries no idata (e.g. a test stub), in which case
    the caller trusts the requested replicate count.
    """
    idata = getattr(fitted, "idata", None)
    posterior = getattr(idata, "posterior", None)
    if posterior is None:
        return None
    return int(posterior.sizes["chain"]) * int(posterior.sizes["draw"])


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Directory evaluation (what the agent / CLI calls)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


def _benjamini_hochberg(pvals: List[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Benjamini-Hochberg step-up FDR-adjusted q-values, in the input order.

    NaN entries (statistics that errored) pass through as NaN and are excluded
    from the correction's m. Each returned q is clipped to ``[0, 1]`` and made
    monotone non-decreasing in p under the standard step-up.
    """
    finite = [
        i for i, p in enumerate(pvals) if isinstance(p, float) and math.isfinite(p)
    ]
    m = len(finite)
    q = [float("nan")] * len(pvals)
    if m == 0:
        return q
    order = sorted(finite, key=lambda i: pvals[i])  # ascending p
    running_min = 1.0
    for rank in range(m - 1, -1, -1):  # step up from the largest p
        i = order[rank]
        running_min = min(running_min, pvals[i] * m / (rank + 1))
        q[i] = min(1.0, running_min)
    return q


def _result_to_dict(res: TestStatisticResult, alpha: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """JSON-serialisable summary of a result (the full null vector is omitted)."""
    t_null = np.asarray(res.t_null, dtype=float) if res.t_null else np.array([])
    significant = (
        res.error is None and not math.isnan(res.p_value) and res.p_value <= alpha
    )
    return {
        "name": res.test_statistic.name,
        "description": res.test_statistic.description,
        "t_observed": res.t_observed,
        "null_mean": float(t_null.mean()) if t_null.size else float("nan"),
        "null_std": float(t_null.std()) if t_null.size else float("nan"),
        "n_replicates": int(t_null.size),
        "z_score": res.z_score,
        "p_value": res.p_value,
        "p_value_one_sided": res.p_value_one_sided,
        "p_value_is_floor": res.p_value_is_floor,
        "significant": bool(significant),
        "error": res.error,
        "code": res.test_statistic.code,
    }


def evaluate_test_stat_dir(
    fitted: Any,
    responses_path: Path,
    test_stats_dir: Path,
    *,
    n_replicates: int,
    seed: int = 42,
    significance_alpha: float = 0.05,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Evaluate every ``test_stats_dir/*.py`` statistic under the PPC.

    Builds the observed + replicate frames once, runs every statistic, and
    returns a JSON-serialisable dict with one entry per statistic (sorted
    most-discrepant first) plus a significance count (raw two-sided p ≤ alpha;
    no multiple-comparisons correction). Fails loudly if the directory holds no
    test-statistic files.
    """
    test_stats_dir = Path(test_stats_dir)
    stat_files = sorted(test_stats_dir.glob("*.py"))
    if not stat_files:
        raise ValueError(f"No test-statistic .py files in {test_stats_dir}")

    human_df, model_dfs = build_critique_frames(
        fitted, responses_path, n_replicates=n_replicates, seed=seed
    )
    return score_statistics(
        fitted.name, human_df, model_dfs, stat_files, significance_alpha=significance_alpha
    )


def score_statistics(
    model_name: str,
    human_df: Any,
    model_dfs: Any,
    stat_files: List[Path],
    *,
    significance_alpha: float = 0.05,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Score statistic files on observed and replicate frames (any domain).

    ``model_dfs`` is a sized iterable of replicate frames (a list, or a lazy
    sequence that builds each frame when iterated: the RSA domain,
    `src.rsa.loop.critique`). Returns `evaluate_test_stat_dir`'s dict.
    """
    statistics = [load_test_statistic_file(p) for p in stat_files]
    results = [evaluate_test_statistic(ts, human_df, model_dfs) for ts in statistics]

    rows = [_result_to_dict(r, significance_alpha) for r in results]
    # Multiple statistics are screened per round, so also report a Benjamini-
    # Hochberg FDR-adjusted q-value and flag alongside the raw p. ``significant``
    # stays the raw screen (kept for back-compat / the most-discrepant sort);
    # ``significant_fdr`` is the multiplicity-aware view.
    qvals = _benjamini_hochberg([d["p_value"] for d in rows])
    for d, q in zip(rows, qvals):
        d["p_value_fdr"] = q
        d["significant_fdr"] = bool(
            d["error"] is None
            and isinstance(q, float)
            and math.isfinite(q)
            and q <= significance_alpha
        )
    # Most discrepant first: significant before not, then by |z|.
    rows.sort(
        key=lambda d: (
            not d["significant"],
            -(abs(d["z_score"]) if math.isfinite(d["z_score"]) else math.inf),
        )
    )
    return {
        "model": model_name,
        "n_test_statistics": len(rows),
        "n_replicates": len(model_dfs),
        "significance_alpha": significance_alpha,
        "n_significant": sum(1 for d in rows if d["significant"]),
        "n_significant_fdr": sum(1 for d in rows if d["significant_fdr"]),
        "results": rows,
    }


def run_ppc_for_model(
    model_name: str,
    models_dir: Path,
    responses_path: Path,
    test_stats_dir: Path,
    *,
    cache_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
    n_replicates: int = 200,
    seed: int = 42,
    significance_alpha: float = 0.05,
    fit_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Fit (or reuse a cached fit of) ``model_name`` and run the PPC critique.

    The fit reuses the same MCMC cache the inner loop wrote, so when called right
    after the inner loop scored the model set this adds no new sampling.
    """
    from src.models.pymc_inference import fit_models_cached

    fit_kwargs = fit_kwargs or {}
    fits = fit_models_cached(
        [model_name],
        models_dir=Path(models_dir),
        responses_path=Path(responses_path),
        cache_dir=cache_dir,
        **fit_kwargs,
    )
    return evaluate_test_stat_dir(
        fits[model_name],
        responses_path,
        test_stats_dir,
        n_replicates=n_replicates,
        seed=seed,
        significance_alpha=significance_alpha,
    )


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# CLI
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────


@dataclass
class Args:
    """Run a posterior-predictive critique of one fitted PyMC model."""

    responses: Path
    """Path to the pooled responses CSV the model was fit on."""
    model: str
    """Incumbent model name (``<model>.py`` must exist in --models-dir)."""
    models_dir: Path
    """Directory holding the model set (the inner loop's ``model_loop/models``)."""
    test_stats_dir: Path
    """Directory of ``test_statistic(df)`` ``.py`` files the agent wrote."""
    out: Optional[Path] = None
    """Write the results JSON here (default: stdout)."""
    cache_dir: Optional[Path] = None
    """MCMC fit cache to reuse (share the inner loop's so no refit is needed)."""
    n_replicates: int = 200
    """Posterior-predictive replicates forming each statistic's null distribution."""
    significance_alpha: float = 0.05
    """Raw two-sided p-value threshold for flagging a statistic as a significant
    discrepancy (no multiple-comparisons correction)."""
    seed: int = 42
    """Seed for posterior-predictive sampling."""
    draws: int = PRODUCTION_DRAWS
    """MCMC draws (only used if the fit is not already cached;
    src.models.mcmc_defaults)."""
    tune: int = PRODUCTION_TUNE
    """MCMC tuning steps (only used if the fit is not already cached)."""
    chains: int = PRODUCTION_CHAINS
    """MCMC chains (only used if the fit is not already cached)."""


def main(args: Args) -> None:
    """CLI entry point: run the posterior-predictive critique and write results as JSON."""
    if not args.responses.exists():
        print(f"Error: responses not found: {args.responses}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    result = run_ppc_for_model(
        args.model,
        args.models_dir,
        args.responses,
        args.test_stats_dir,
        cache_dir=args.cache_dir,
        n_replicates=args.n_replicates,
        seed=args.seed,
        significance_alpha=args.significance_alpha,
        fit_kwargs={"draws": args.draws, "tune": args.tune, "chains": args.chains},
    )

    output = json.dumps(result, indent=2)
    if args.out:
        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.out.write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
        print(
            f"Wrote {args.out} — {result['n_significant']}/{result['n_test_statistics']} "
            f"test statistics significant at p ≤ {result['significance_alpha']} "
            f"({result['n_replicates']} PPC replicates)",
            flush=True,
        )
    else:
        print(output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import tyro

    main(tyro.cli(Args))

"""Shepard-Tversky similarity-crowded pragmatic listener and speaker.

Candidate referents with similar feature vectors and candidate words with similar
scene extensions crowd each other according to an exponential similarity kernel
exp(-gamma * d). Inside the communicative hierarchy, listeners divide reference
weight across each object's perceptual similarity cluster (1 / obj_crowding) and
speakers divide lexical choice weight across each word's extension similarity
cluster among words true of the target (1 / utt_crowding). At the top level and
on wordless prior trials, listeners favor perceptually uncrowded pop-out referents
proportional to obj_crowding ** (-beta).
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, vec

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "beta": dist.LogNormal(0.5, 0.5),
    "gamma": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 0.75),
}


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ..., inv_obj_crowd: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r) * vec(inv_obj_crowd, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., lex_unif: ..., inv_obj_crowd: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(inv_obj_crowd, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex_unif, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L0[u, r](lex, inv_obj_crowd) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L2[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., lex_unif: ..., inv_obj_crowd: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L1[u, r](alpha, lex, lex_unif, inv_obj_crowd) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def listener(params, ctx):
    gamma = params["gamma"]
    real_mask = 1.0 - ctx.is_sink
    real_lex = ctx.lex * real_mask[:, None]

    obj_diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, :, None] - real_lex[:, None, :])
    obj_dist = jnp.sum(obj_diff, axis=0)
    obj_sim = jnp.exp(-gamma * obj_dist)
    obj_crowding = jnp.sum(obj_sim, axis=1)
    inv_obj_crowd = 1.0 / obj_crowding
    prior = softmax_prior(-params["beta"] * jnp.log(obj_crowding))

    utt_diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, None, :] - real_lex[None, :, :])
    utt_dist = jnp.sum(utt_diff, axis=2)
    utt_sim = jnp.exp(-gamma * utt_dist) * (real_mask[:, None] * real_mask[None, :])
    utt_crowding = jnp.maximum(utt_sim @ real_lex, 1.0)
    lex_unif = ctx.lex / utt_crowding

    heard = L2(params["alpha"], ctx.lex, lex_unif, inv_obj_crowd, prior)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0 by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:

"""RSA pragmatic listener at depth 2 with singleton salience, contextual distinctiveness, visual feature complexity, evaluative valence framing, visual color contrast, and literal L0.

Refining rsa_l2_singleton_distinct_feat_color_l0 by incorporating the evaluative valence framing component from polarity_congruence_listener:
speakers and listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a depth-1 pragmatic listener) with
common knowledge of an object prior combining discrete visual singleton salience (favoring unique objects with
no duplicates in the scene), continuous contextual distinctiveness (favoring objects with greater feature contrast
relative to the rest of the display), visual feature complexity modulated by evaluative framing valence (favoring
feature-rich items under neutral/positive framing but inverting to favor sparse, featureless items when referring
to a least favorite object), and visual color contrast (favoring fully colored objects over desaturated grayscale
distractors). Crucially, the foundational simulated literal listener L0 operates purely on truth-conditional semantics
without perceptual bias, preventing redundant prior compounding across reasoning tiers. On prior trials with no
informative word, choices are governed directly by the combined perceptual prior. A lapse parameter mixes in uniform guessing.
"""

import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpyro.distributions as dist
from memo import memo

from src.rsa.memo_kit import EPS, at, softmax_prior, vec, with_lapse

PARAMS = {
    "alpha": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_singleton": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_distinct": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_features": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_valence": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
    "w_color": dist.Normal(0.0, 1.0),
}


@memo
def L0[u: UTT, r: OBJ](lex: ...):
    listener: knows(u)
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=at(lex, u, r))
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L1[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L0[u, r](lex) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


@memo
def L2[u: UTT, r: OBJ](alpha, lex: ..., prior: ...):
    listener: thinks[
        speaker: given(r in OBJ, wpp=vec(prior, r)),
        speaker: chooses(
            u in UTT,
            wpp=at(lex, u, r)
            * exp(alpha * log(L1[u, r](alpha, lex, prior) + {EPS})),
        ),
    ]
    listener: observes [speaker.u] is u
    listener: chooses(r in OBJ, wpp=Pr[speaker.r == r])
    return Pr[listener.r == r]


def listener(params, ctx):
    diffs = jnp.abs(ctx.lex[:, :, None] - ctx.lex[:, None, :])
    pair_dist = jnp.sum(diffs * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None, None]), axis=0)
    gray_diff = jnp.abs(ctx.grayscale[:, None] - ctx.grayscale[None, :])
    fam_diff = jnp.abs(
        ctx.familiarization[:, None] - ctx.familiarization[None, :]
    )
    total_dist = pair_dist + gray_diff + fam_diff
    duplicate_count = jnp.sum(total_dist == 0, axis=1)
    is_singleton = jnp.where(duplicate_count == 1, 1.0, 0.0)

    real_lex = ctx.lex * (1.0 - ctx.is_sink[:, None])
    diff = jnp.abs(real_lex[:, :, None] - real_lex[:, None, :])
    distinct = jnp.sum(diff, axis=(0, 2))

    effective_w_features = (
        params["w_features"] + ctx.valence * params["w_valence"]
    )

    prior = softmax_prior(
        params["w_singleton"] * is_singleton
        + params["w_distinct"] * distinct
        + effective_w_features * ctx.feature_count
        + params["w_color"] * (1.0 - ctx.grayscale)
    )

    heard = L2(params["alpha"], ctx.lex, prior)[ctx.utterance]
    return jnp.where(ctx.is_prior > 0, prior, heard)

            sampled = link.sample(k, lat[r], lp, probes[g.indices], g.arrays, utterances[g.indices], **extra)
            for i, s in zip(g.indices, sampled):
                cells = _flat(s)
                row[i] = _cell(cells[columns[0]]) if len(columns) == 1 else tuple(_cell(cells[c]) for c in columns)
        out.append(row)
    return out


class ReplicateFrames:
    """The replicate frames, built one at a time when iterated (only the outcome column differs;
    with several ``column``s, each outcome is a tuple of their values)."""

    def __init__(self, observed: pd.DataFrame, column, outcomes: List[List[Any]]) -> None:
        if outcomes and len(outcomes[0]) != len(observed):
            raise ValueError(f"{len(outcomes[0])} simulated responses per replicate for {len(observed)} trials")
        self.observed, self.column, self.outcomes = observed, column, outcomes

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.outcomes)

    def __iter__(self):
        for row in self.outcomes:
            df = self.observed.copy()
            if isinstance(self.column, str):
                df[self.column] = row
            else:
                for j, c in enumerate(self.column):
                    df[c] = [v[j] for v in row]
            yield df


def context_md(*, critique_dir: Path, incumbent: str, incumbent_file: Path, hypothesis: str, block: Block,
               paradigm_note: str, data_path: Path, observed: pd.DataFrame, n_proposals: int, alpha: float,
               n_replicates: int) -> str:
    from src.critique.ppc import _TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC, _TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC

    design = [c for c in ("probe", "target", "second_probe", "second_target") if c in observed.columns]
    if block.link.name == "binary_judgment":
        design.append("utterance")
    if "second_utterance" in observed.columns:
        design.append("second_utterance")
    n_scenes = observed[["objects", "heard"]].astype(str).drop_duplicates().shape[0]
    return f"""# Critique context

**Incumbent (best) theory:** `{incumbent}`
**Its code:** `{incumbent_file}`
**Its hypothesis:** {hypothesis.strip() or "(no stated hypothesis)"}

**The experiment critiqued:** `{block.name}`, the newest one (the loop selects theories on it).
{paradigm_note}
Its link (response process): `{block.link.name}`.

**The data your statistics receive:** {len(observed)} trials (rows) over {n_scenes} distinct scenes
(`objects` x `heard`), as in `{data_path}`, with these columns: `{", ".join(observed.columns)}`.
- `objects`: a JSON list of 0/1 feature lists, one per object.
- `heard`: the index of the feature whose word was heard (NaN when no word was heard).
- `unit`: the designed trial the row belongs to.{"" if not design else chr(10) + "- " + ", ".join(f"`{c}`" for c in design) + ": the trial's design (as presented, the same in every simulated dataset)."}
- **The response:** {outcome_words(block.link)}.

**Your job:** propose **{n_proposals}** test statistics. Write each to
`{critique_dir / "test_stats"}/<name>.py` as `test_statistic(df)` returning one
float, with `# name:` and `# description:` header comments.

You do not need to run anything: the pipeline computes each statistic on the
observed data and on {n_replicates} datasets simulated from the incumbent's
posterior through this experiment's link (only {", ".join(f"`{c}`" for c in outcome_columns(block.link))} differ{"s" if len(outcome_columns(block.link)) == 1 else ""} between them),
and flags a statistic as a **significant discrepancy** when its two-sided p ≤ {alpha}
(with a Benjamini–Hochberg q beside it).

**Time:** each statistic is called {n_replicates + 1} times. Each call must finish
within {_TEST_STAT_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC:g} s and all of them within {_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC:g} s
(about {_TEST_STAT_BUDGET_SEC / (n_replicates + 1):.2g} s per call on {len(observed)} rows).
Compute scene properties once per distinct scene and map them onto the rows; a
statistic that is too slow, raises or returns a non-finite value is set aside and
reported back to you.
"""


def build_prompt(critique_dir: Path, context_text: str, *, attempt: int = 0,
                 broken: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> str:
    from src.rsa.loop import critique as closed

    text = closed.build_prompt(critique_dir, context_text, attempt=attempt, broken=broken)
    old = closed.PROMPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if not text.startswith(old):
        raise RuntimeError("the closed critique prompt changed shape; update src.rsa_open.loop.critique")
    return PROMPT.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + text[len(old):]


def run_critique(round_dir: Path, *, spawn: SpawnFn, incumbent: str, theory: TheoryModel, fitted: CorpusFit,
                 hypothesis: str, incumbent_file: Path, block: Block, paradigm_note: str, data_path: Path,
                 n_proposals: int = CRITIQUE_N_PROPOSALS, alpha: float = CRITIQUE_SIGNIFICANCE_ALPHA,
                 n_replicates: int = CRITIQUE_PPC_REPLICATES, seed: int = 0) -> CritiqueOutcome:
    """Critique the incumbent on ``block`` before a candidate round (the closed critic's rules: one
    retry; a round whose statistics all fail, or none are written, has no critique, recorded)."""
    from src.critique.ppc import score_statistics
    from src.pipelines.inner_loop.critique_round import _format_critiques_md, _usable_test_statistics

    observed = critique_frame(block)
    broken: Dict[str, str] = {}
    usable: List[Path] = []
    cdir = round_dir / "critique"
    attempts = 0
    for attempt in range(1 + MAX_CRITIQUE_RETRIES):
        attempts = attempt + 1
        cdir = round_dir / ("critique" if attempt == 0 else f"critique_retry_{attempt}")
        cdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        text = context_md(critique_dir=cdir, incumbent=incumbent, incumbent_file=incumbent_file,
                          hypothesis=hypothesis, block=block, paradigm_note=paradigm_note, data_path=data_path,
                          observed=observed, n_proposals=n_proposals, alpha=alpha, n_replicates=n_replicates)
        (cdir / "CRITIQUE_CONTEXT.md").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        spawn(cdir, build_prompt(cdir, text, attempt=attempt, broken=broken))
        usable, broken = _usable_test_statistics(cdir / "test_stats", observed, n_replicates=n_replicates)
        if usable:
            break
        print(f"  [critique] attempt {attempts}: no usable test statistic in {cdir / 'test_stats'}", flush=True)
    if not usable:
        reason = f"the critique agent wrote no usable test statistic in {attempts} attempts"
        print(f"  [critique] NO CRITIQUE this round: {reason}", flush=True)
        return CritiqueOutcome(None, dict(status=CRITIQUE_STATUS_NONE, incumbent=incumbent, attempts=attempts,
                                          reason=reason, broken=broken))
    columns = outcome_columns(block.link)
    reps = ReplicateFrames(observed, columns[0] if len(columns) == 1 else columns,
                           simulate_outcomes(theory, fitted, block, n_replicates, seed))
    result = score_statistics(incumbent, observed, reps, usable, significance_alpha=alpha)
    result["n_replicates"] = len(reps)
    (cdir / "ppc_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    md = _format_critiques_md(result)
    (cdir / "critiques.md").write_text(md, encoding="utf-8")
    n_evaluated = sum(1 for r in result["results"] if not r.get("error"))
    print(f"  [critique] {result['n_significant']} of {n_evaluated} evaluated statistics show a significant "
          "discrepancy", flush=True)
    if n_evaluated == 0:
        reason = ("none of the test statistics produced a p-value: "
                  + "; ".join(f"{r['name']}: {r['error']}" for r in result["results"]))
        return CritiqueOutcome(None, dict(status=CRITIQUE_STATUS_NONE, incumbent=incumbent, attempts=attempts,
                                          reason=reason))
    return CritiqueOutcome(md, dict(
        status=CRITIQUE_STATUS_CRITIQUED, incumbent=incumbent, attempts=attempts, dir=str(cdir), block=block.name,
        n_statistics=int(result["n_test_statistics"]), n_evaluated=n_evaluated,
        n_significant=int(result["n_significant"]), n_significant_fdr=int(result["n_significant_fdr"])))

1: """Links: from a theory's latent quantities to the likelihood of one response type
2: (docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3).
3: 
4: A theory is paradigm-free: it defines ``PARAMS`` and ``listener(params, ctx)``, the listener's
5: posterior over the objects of one scene. A link is a response process with its own parameters,
6: shared by every theory on a paradigm and frozen with the paradigm before any data. Theorists
7: never write links.
8: 
9: Each link has a **likelihood** (`likelihood`): its parameters' priors, a check of each
10: response, the log-likelihood of a group of trials given the theory's latent posteriors, and a
11: simulator. `src.rsa_open.fit` fits any theory under any link with it.
12: 
13: Every link shares one response process (PI 2026-10-21; `src.rsa_open.link_kit`): the posterior
14: is **tempered** (``temperature``, a decision temperature: p ** temperature, renormalized; prior
15: LogNormal(0, 0.5), median 1) and then mixed with a uniform guess with probability ``lapse``
16: (prior Beta(1, 9)). Then, per link:
17: 
18: - **choice**: pick one referent; summed over classes of identical objects (the closed
19:   campaign's likelihood, which is this link at temperature 1).
20: - **rating**: rate how likely a probed referent is, on a ``scale_points`` scale. An ordered
21:   probit on the logit of the tempered probability, with equally spaced cutpoints (``center``,
22:   ``spread``); the lapse is a uniform rating.
23: - **allocation**: split ``total_points`` points over the referents (a bet). A
24:   Dirichlet-multinomial with concentration ``kappa`` times the tempered, lapse-mixed
25:   posterior: the discrete counterpart of a Dirichlet, exact for integer bets, with zeros as
26:   ordinary outcomes. This is the betting measure of Frank & Goodman (2012); the paradigm
27:   response type is ``bet``.
28: - **ordered_beta**: one slider (or bet) from 0 to ``total_points`` on a probed referent
29:   (Kubinec, 2022): with ``eta`` the logit of its tempered probability q, P(0) = 1 - σ(eta - k1)
30:   and P(max) = σ(eta - k2), with cutpoints k1 = ``cut_low`` and k2 = k1 + ``cut_gap``; the
31:   interior values 1..max-1 share P(interior) as a **discrete Beta**: proportional to the
32:   Beta(q φ, (1 - q) φ) density at v / max (``phi``, the precision), normalized over them, so the
33:   slider's max + 1 positions get an exact distribution (a density times 1 / max would not be
34:   one: near 0 or 1 a Beta's mass sits between the slider's steps). The lapse is uniform over the
35:   max + 1 positions. The paradigm response type is ``slider``. For the design tool the same
36:   distribution is binned (`SLIDER_BINS`): coarsening can only lose information, so the tool's
37:   score is a lower bound.
38: 
39: The speaker-side links score the theory's **speaker** (`src.rsa_open.fit.TheoryModel`): its own
40: ``speaker(params, ctx)`` if it defines one, else the speaker derived from its listener
41: (PI 2026-10-21). Their responses name a ``target`` object and an ``utterance``, an index into
42: the scene's real messages (never the sink).
43: 
44: - **production**: choose a message for a target. The tempered speaker distribution over the
45:   real messages, mixed with a uniform choice among them (``lapse``).
46: - **binary_judgment**: "would the speaker say this message for this one?" The rating link at
47:   two points on the tempered speaker probability: P(yes) = Φ(logit(q) - ``center``), with a
48:   random yes/no lapse.
49: 
50: **Two measures** (PI 2026-10-26): a paradigm may ask a second question about the same screen
51: (`PairLikelihood`, the ``pair`` link). Both parts read the same side of the theory (its listener,
52: or its speaker), their responses are independent given it, so the pair's log-likelihood is the
53: sum of the parts' and its outcomes, for the design tool, are their product (at most
54: ``MAX_PAIR_OUTCOMES``). The second part's parameters carry the prefix ``q2_`` (its own temperature,
55: lapse, ...), its trial fields the prefix ``second_`` (``second_probe``, ``second_target``,
56: ``second_utterance``), and its response sits in the first's as ``"second"``. A second measure is
57: small: a choice or a rating of at most ``MAX_SECOND_POINTS`` points after a listener measure, a
58: yes/no judgment after a speaker measure (`SECOND_TYPES`).
59: 
60: The choice link also has a **model-file form**: `compose` puts a theory and the link together
61: into an ordinary RSA model file (``PARAMS`` and ``choice_probs``), so the closed campaign's
62: fitting, cross-validation and loop code runs it unchanged. The link's parameters are appended
63: to the theory's, so a theory may not use their names (`LinkClash`).
64: """

150: def _safe_log(p: jnp.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:

155: def rating_probs(p, center, spread, lapse, points: int) -> jnp.ndarray:
156:     """(..., points) probability of each rating 1..points given the probed referent's
157:     (tempered) probability p."""
158:     q = jnp.clip(jnp.asarray(p), RATING_CLIP, 1.0 - RATING_CLIP)
159:     eta = jnp.log(q) - jnp.log1p(-q)
160:     cuts = center + spread * (jnp.arange(1, points) - points / 2.0)

162:     zeros, ones = jnp.zeros_like(cdf[..., :1]), jnp.ones_like(cdf[..., :1])

287:             if any(not isinstance(x, (int, np.integer)) for x in pts) or any(x < 0 for x in pts):
288:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: points must be non-negative integers, none negative; got {pts}")
289:             if sum(pts) != total:
290:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: points must sum to {total}; got {sum(pts)}")
291:             return {"points": [int(x) for x in pts]}
292:         if self.name == "ordered_beta":
293:             top, r = self.options["total_points"], response.get("probe")
294:             if not isinstance(r, (int, np.integer)) or not 0 <= r < n:
295:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a slider response needs 'probe', an object index "
296:                                  f"0..{n - 1}; got {dict(response)}")
297:             v = response.get("value")
298:             if not isinstance(v, (int, np.integer)) or not 0 <= v <= top:
299:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a slider value must be an integer between 0 and {top}; got {v!r}")
300:             return {"probe": int(r), "value": int(v)}
301:         if self.name in SPEAKER_LINKS:
302:             n_utt = ctx.shape[1]
303:             n_real = n_utt - (1 if ctx.needs_sink else 0)
304:             t, u = response.get("target"), response.get("utterance")
305:             if not isinstance(t, (int, np.integer)) or not 0 <= t < n:
306:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a {self.name} response needs 'target', an object index "
307:                                  f"0..{n - 1}; got {dict(response)}")
308:             if not isinstance(u, (int, np.integer)) or not 0 <= u < n_utt:
309:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a {self.name} response needs 'utterance', a message index "
310:                                  f"0..{n_real - 1}; got {dict(response)}")
311:             if u >= n_real:
312:                 raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: utterance {u} is the scene's sink ('no word applies'), "
313:                                  f"which no speaker says; the real messages are 0..{n_real - 1}")
314:             out = {"target": int(t), "utterance": int(u)}
315:             if self.name == "binary_judgment":
316:                 a = response.get("answer")
317:                 if not isinstance(a, bool):
318:                     raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a judgment needs 'answer', true or false; got {a!r}")
319:                 out["answer"] = int(a)
320:             return out
321:         raise KeyError(self.name)

323:     def stack(self, encoded: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, jnp.ndarray]:
324:         keys = encoded[0].keys()
325:         return {k: jnp.asarray(np.asarray([e[k] for e in encoded])) for k in keys}

328:     def log_lik(self, latent: jnp.ndarray, p: Mapping[str, Any], enc: Mapping[str, jnp.ndarray],
329:                 arrays, classes) -> jnp.ndarray:
330:         """(trials,) log-likelihood of each response. ``latent`` is (trials, N_OBJ) listener
331:         posteriors, or for a speaker link (trials, N_UTT, N_OBJ) speaker distributions;
332:         ``arrays`` are the trials' scene arrays and ``classes`` their choice classes."""
333:         if self.name == "choice":
334:             from src.rsa.fit import class_probs
335: 
336:             cp = class_probs(with_uniform(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), p["lapse"]), classes)
337:             return _safe_log(jnp.take_along_axis(cp, enc["cls"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0])
338:         if self.name == "rating":
339:             tempered = temper(latent, p["temperature"])
340:             pr = jnp.take_along_axis(tempered, enc["probe"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
341:             probs = rating_probs(pr, p["center"], p["spread"], p["lapse"], self.options["scale_points"])
342:             return jnp.log(jnp.take_along_axis(probs, enc["rating"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0])
343:         if self.name == "allocation":
344:             return allocation_log_prob(latent, enc["points"].astype(latent.dtype),
345:                                        self.options["total_points"], p["kappa"], p["lapse"], p["temperature"])
346:         if self.name == "ordered_beta":
347:             q = jnp.take_along_axis(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), enc["probe"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
348:             return ordered_beta_log_prob(q, enc["value"], self.options["total_points"], p)
349:         if self.name in SPEAKER_LINKS:
350:             if self.name == "production":
351:                 dist_u = _speaker_choice(latent, enc["target"], arrays.is_sink, p)
352:                 return _safe_log(jnp.take_along_axis(dist_u, enc["utterance"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0])
353:             q = jnp.take_along_axis(_tempered_speaker(latent, enc["target"], arrays.is_sink, p),
354:                                     enc["utterance"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
355:             probs = rating_probs(q, p["center"], 1.0, p["lapse"], 2)
356:             return jnp.log(jnp.take_along_axis(probs, enc["answer"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0])
357:         raise KeyError(self.name)

363:     def outcome_probs(self, latent: jnp.ndarray, p: Mapping[str, Any], unit: Mapping[str, jnp.ndarray],
364:                       arrays, classes) -> jnp.ndarray:
365:         """(units, W): the probability of each outcome of each trial unit; ``unit`` holds a
366:         unit's response fields other than the outcome itself (a probe, a target, a message).
367:         log of entry k is `log_lik` of the response `outcome_response(k)`."""
368:         if self.name == "choice":
369:             from src.rsa.fit import class_probs
370: 
371:             return class_probs(with_uniform(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), p["lapse"]), classes)
372:         if self.name == "rating":
373:             tempered = temper(latent, p["temperature"])
374:             pr = jnp.take_along_axis(tempered, unit["probe"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
375:             return rating_probs(pr, p["center"], p["spread"], p["lapse"], self.options["scale_points"])
376:         if self.name == "ordered_beta":
377:             q = jnp.take_along_axis(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), unit["probe"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
378:             return ordered_beta_bin_probs(q, self.options["total_points"], p)
379:         if self.name == "production":
380:             return _speaker_choice(latent, unit["target"], arrays.is_sink, p)
381:         if self.name == "binary_judgment":
382:             q = jnp.take_along_axis(_tempered_speaker(latent, unit["target"], arrays.is_sink, p),
383:                                     unit["utterance"][:, None], axis=1)[:, 0]
384:             return rating_probs(q, p["center"], 1.0, p["lapse"], 2)
385:         if self.name == "allocation":
386:             n = latent.shape[1]
387:             t = design_bet_total(n, self.options["total_points"])
388:             comps = jnp.asarray(bet_compositions(n, t), dtype=latent.dtype)  # (W, n)
389:             ll = allocation_log_prob(latent[:, None, :], comps[None], t, p["kappa"], p["lapse"], p["temperature"])
390:             return jnp.exp(ll)
391:         raise NotImplementedError(
392:             f"the {self.name!r} link's outcomes are not categorical; the design tool cannot score it yet")

394:     def outcome_valid(self, arrays, classes, unit: Mapping[str, jnp.ndarray]) -> jnp.ndarray:
395:         """(units, W) bool: the outcome slots that exist for each unit."""
396:         if self.name == "choice":
397:             c = jnp.asarray(classes)
398:             return c == jnp.arange(c.shape[1])[None, :]  # a class sits at its first object
399:         if self.name == "rating":
400:             return jnp.ones((unit["probe"].shape[0], self.options["scale_points"]), dtype=bool)
401:         if self.name == "ordered_beta":
402:             return jnp.ones((unit["probe"].shape[0], len(slider_bin_edges(self.options["total_points"])) + 1),
403:                             dtype=bool)
404:         if self.name == "production":
405:             return arrays.is_sink < 0.5
406:         if self.name == "binary_judgment":
407:             return jnp.ones((unit["target"].shape[0], 2), dtype=bool)
408:         if self.name == "allocation":
409:             n = jnp.asarray(classes).shape[1]
410:             w = len(bet_compositions(n, design_bet_total(n, self.options["total_points"])))
411:             return jnp.ones((jnp.asarray(classes).shape[0], w), dtype=bool)
412:         raise NotImplementedError(self.name)

415:         """The encoded response fields that name outcome slot ``k``."""

417:                       "binary_judgment": "answer"}[self.name]

420:     # -- simulation
421:     def sample(self, key, latent: np.ndarray, p: Mapping[str, Any], probes: np.ndarray,
422:                arrays=None, utterances: Optional[np.ndarray] = None) -> List[dict]:
423:         """One response per trial. ``probes`` are the probed (rating) or target (speaker) objects;
424:         ``utterances`` the messages judged (binary_judgment)."""
425:         latent = jnp.asarray(latent)
426:         if self.name == "choice":
427:             picks = jax.random.categorical(
428:                 key, _safe_log(with_uniform(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), p["lapse"])), axis=-1)
429:             return [{"choice": int(c)} for c in np.asarray(picks)]
430:         if self.name == "rating":
431:             tempered = temper(latent, p["temperature"])
432:             pr = tempered[jnp.arange(latent.shape[0]), jnp.asarray(probes)]
433:             probs = rating_probs(pr, p["center"], p["spread"], p["lapse"], self.options["scale_points"])
434:             ratings = jax.random.categorical(key, jnp.log(probs), axis=-1)
435:             return [{"probe": int(r), "rating": int(v) + 1} for r, v in zip(probes, np.asarray(ratings))]
436:         if self.name == "allocation":
437:             conc = jnp.maximum(p["kappa"] * with_uniform(temper(latent, p["temperature"]), p["lapse"]),
438:                                CONCENTRATION_FLOOR)
439:             pts = dist.DirichletMultinomial(conc, total_count=self.options["total_points"]).sample(key)
440:             return [{"points": [int(x) for x in row]} for row in np.asarray(pts)]
441:         if self.name == "ordered_beta":
442:             top = self.options["total_points"]
443:             q = temper(latent, p["temperature"])[jnp.arange(latent.shape[0]), jnp.asarray(probes)]
444:             values = np.asarray(jax.random.categorical(key, jnp.log(ordered_beta_pmf(q, top, p)), axis=-1))
445:             return [{"probe": int(r), "value": int(v)} for r, v in zip(probes, values)]
446:         if self.name == "production":
447:             dist_u = _speaker_choice(latent, jnp.asarray(probes), arrays.is_sink, p)
448:             said = jax.random.categorical(key, _safe_log(dist_u), axis=-1)
449:             return [{"target": int(t), "utterance": int(u)} for t, u in zip(probes, np.asarray(said))]
450:         if self.name == "binary_judgment":
451:             q = _tempered_speaker(latent, jnp.asarray(probes), arrays.is_sink, p)[
452:                 jnp.arange(latent.shape[0]), jnp.asarray(utterances)]
453:             yes = jax.random.uniform(key, q.shape) < rating_probs(q, p["center"], 1.0, p["lapse"], 2)[:, 1]
454:             return [{"target": int(t), "utterance": int(u), "answer": bool(a)}
455:                     for t, u, a in zip(probes, utterances, np.asarray(yes))]
456:         raise KeyError(self.name)

459: SECOND_PREFIX = "q2_"  # the second measure's parameters
460: SECOND_ENC = "q2."  # its encoded response fields
461: SECOND_FIELDS = {"probe": "second_probe", "target": "second_target", "utterance": "second_utterance"}
462: SECOND_TYPES = {"listener": ("choice", "rating"), "speaker": ("binary_judgment",)}
463: MAX_SECOND_POINTS = 7

467: @dataclass(frozen=True)
468: class PairLikelihood:
469:     """Two measures of one screen (see the module's docstring): the parts' likelihoods summed."""
470: 
471:     first: LinkLikelihood
472:     second: LinkLikelihood
473:     name: str = "pair"
474: 
475:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
476:         if self.first.side != self.second.side:
477:             raise ValueError(f"a pair's measures read one side of the theory: {self.first.name} reads its "
478:                              f"{self.first.side}, {self.second.name} its {self.second.side}")
479:         if self.second.name not in SECOND_TYPES[self.first.side]:
480:             raise ValueError(f"after a {self.first.side} measure the second is one of "
481:                              f"{SECOND_TYPES[self.first.side]}, not {self.second.name}")
482: 
483:     @property
484:     def side(self) -> str:
485:         return self.first.side
486: 
487:     @property
488:     def response_type(self) -> str:
489:         return f"{self.first.response_type}+{self.second.response_type}"
490: 
491:     @property
492:     def params(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
493:         return {**self.first.params, **{SECOND_PREFIX + k: v for k, v in self.second.params.items()}}
494: 
495:     @property
496:     def reference_params(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
497:         return {**self.first.reference_params,
498:                 **{SECOND_PREFIX + k: v for k, v in self.second.reference_params.items()}}
499: 
500:     @property
501:     def options(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
502:         return {"first": {"name": self.first.name, **self.first.options},
503:                 "second": {"name": self.second.name, **self.second.options}}
504: 
505:     def named_params(self, by_link: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]]) -> Dict[str, float]:
506:         return {**self.first.named_params(by_link),
507:                 **{SECOND_PREFIX + k: v for k, v in self.second.named_params(by_link).items()}}
508: 
509:     def _p(self, p: Mapping[str, Any]):
510:         return ({k: p[k] for k in self.first.params},
511:                 {k: p[SECOND_PREFIX + k] for k in self.second.params})
512: 
513:     @staticmethod
514:     def _enc(enc: Mapping[str, Any]):
515:         return ({k: v for k, v in enc.items() if not k.startswith(SECOND_ENC)},
516:                 {k[len(SECOND_ENC):]: v for k, v in enc.items() if k.startswith(SECOND_ENC)})
517: 
518:     @staticmethod
519:     def _unit(unit: Mapping[str, Any]):
520:         second = {v: k for k, v in SECOND_FIELDS.items()}
521:         return ({k: v for k, v in unit.items() if k not in second},
522:                 {second[k]: v for k, v in unit.items() if k in second})
523: 
524:     def encode(self, ctx, response: Mapping[str, Any], i: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
525:         r2 = response.get("second")
526:         if not isinstance(r2, Mapping):
527:             raise ValueError(f"trial {i}: a two-measure response needs 'second', the second measure's "
528:                              f"response; got {dict(response)}")
529:         e1 = self.first.encode(ctx, {k: v for k, v in response.items() if k != "second"}, i)
530:         e2 = self.second.encode(ctx, r2, i)
531:         return {**e1, **{SECOND_ENC + k: v for k, v in e2.items()}}
532: 
533:     def stack(self, encoded: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, jnp.ndarray]:
534:         keys = encoded[0].keys()
535:         return {k: jnp.asarray(np.asarray([e[k] for e in encoded])) for k in keys}
536: 
537:     def log_lik(self, latent, p, enc, arrays, classes) -> jnp.ndarray:
538:         (p1, p2), (e1, e2) = self._p(p), self._enc(enc)
539:         return (self.first.log_lik(latent, p1, e1, arrays, classes)
540:                 + self.second.log_lik(latent, p2, e2, arrays, classes))
541: 
542:     def outcome_probs(self, latent, p, unit, arrays, classes) -> jnp.ndarray:
543:         (p1, p2), (u1, u2) = self._p(p), self._unit(unit)
544:         a = self.first.outcome_probs(latent, p1, u1, arrays, classes)
545:         b = self.second.outcome_probs(latent, p2, u2, arrays, classes)
546:         return (a[:, :, None] * b[:, None, :]).reshape(a.shape[0], -1)
547: 
548:     def outcome_valid(self, arrays, classes, unit) -> jnp.ndarray:
549:         u1, u2 = self._unit(unit)
550:         a = self.first.outcome_valid(arrays, classes, u1)
551:         b = self.second.outcome_valid(arrays, classes, u2)
552:         return (a[:, :, None] & b[:, None, :]).reshape(a.shape[0], -1)
553: 
554:     def sample(self, key, latent, p, probes, arrays=None, utterances=None, second_probes=None,
555:                second_utterances=None) -> List[dict]:
556:         """One response per trial, the second measure's under ``"second"``: its probed or target
557:         objects ``second_probes`` and judged messages ``second_utterances`` (default: the first's)."""
558:         (p1, p2), (k1, k2) = self._p(p), jax.random.split(key)
559:         first = self.first.sample(k1, latent, p1, probes, arrays, utterances)
560:         second = self.second.sample(k2, latent, p2, probes if second_probes is None else second_probes, arrays,
561:                                     utterances if second_utterances is None else second_utterances)
562:         return [{**a, "second": b} for a, b in zip(first, second)]

565: def _tempered_speaker(speaker, targets, is_sink, p) -> jnp.ndarray:
566:     """(trials, N_UTT): the tempered speaker distribution over messages for each trial's target."""
567:     column = jnp.take_along_axis(speaker, targets[:, None, None], axis=2)[:, :, 0]
568:     return temper(column * (1.0 - is_sink), p["temperature"])
569: 
570: 
571: def _speaker_choice(speaker, targets, is_sink, p) -> jnp.ndarray:
572:     """(trials, N_UTT): what is said, with the lapse uniform over the real messages."""
573:     real = 1.0 - is_sink
574:     return ((1.0 - p["lapse"]) * _tempered_speaker(speaker, targets, is_sink, p)
575:             + p["lapse"] * real / real.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True))
576:

583:     return {"lapse": dist.Beta(1.0, 9.0), "temperature": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 0.5)}

586: def likelihood(name: str, *, scale_points: Optional[int] = None,
587:                total_points: Optional[int] = None, first: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
588:                second: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None):
589:     """The named link's likelihood, with the options its paradigm fixes; ``pair`` takes its parts
590:     (``first``, ``second``: each a link name and its options)."""
591:     if name == "pair":
592:         if first is None or second is None:
593:             raise ValueError("the pair link needs first and second")
594:         parts = [likelihood(**dict(part)) for part in (first, second)]
595:         return PairLikelihood(*parts)
596:     if name not in LINKS:
597:         raise KeyError(f"no link {name!r}; the library has {sorted(LINKS)}")
598:     link = LINKS[name]
599:     if name == "choice":
600:         return LinkLikelihood(name, link.response_type, {**_shared_params()}, {**SHARED_REFERENCE})
601:     if name == "rating":
602:         if scale_points is None:
603:             raise ValueError("the rating link needs scale_points")
604:         return LinkLikelihood(
605:             name, link.response_type,
606:             {"center": dist.Normal(0.0, 2.0), "spread": dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.0), **_shared_params()},
607:             {"center": 0.0, "spread": 0.8, **SHARED_REFERENCE},
608:             {"scale_points": int(scale_points)})
609:     if name == "allocation":
610:         if total_points is None:
611:             raise ValueError("the allocation link needs total_points")
612:         return LinkLikelihood(
613:             name, link.response_type,
614:             {"kappa": dist.LogNormal(float(np.log(10.0)), 1.0), **_shared_params()},
615:             {"kappa": 10.0, **SHARED_REFERENCE},
616:             {"total_points": int(total_points)})
617:     if name == "ordered_beta":
618:         if total_points is None:
619:             raise ValueError("the ordered_beta link needs total_points (the slider's maximum)")
620:         return LinkLikelihood(
621:             name, link.response_type,
622:             {"cut_low": dist.Normal(-3.0, 1.5), "cut_gap": dist.LogNormal(float(np.log(6.0)), 0.5),
623:              "phi": dist.LogNormal(float(np.log(10.0)), 1.0), **_shared_params()},
624:             {"cut_low": -3.0, "cut_gap": 6.0, "phi": 10.0, **SHARED_REFERENCE},
625:             {"total_points": int(total_points)})
626:     if name == "production":
627:         return LinkLikelihood(name, link.response_type, {**_shared_params()}, {**SHARED_REFERENCE})
628:     if name == "binary_judgment":
629:         return LinkLikelihood(name, link.response_type, {"center": dist.Normal(0.0, 2.0), **_shared_params()},
630:                               {"center": 0.0, **SHARED_REFERENCE})
631:     raise KeyError(name)

636: def _theory_params(tree: ast.Module) -> List[str]:
637:     for node in tree.body:
638:         if (isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and len(node.targets) == 1
639:                 and isinstance(node.targets[0], ast.Name) and node.targets[0].id == "PARAMS"):
640:             if not isinstance(node.value, ast.Dict) or not all(
641:                     isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str) for k in node.value.keys):
642:                 raise ValueError("a theory's PARAMS must be a dict literal with string keys")
643:             return [k.value for k in node.value.keys]
644:     raise ValueError("a theory must define PARAMS")
645:

647: def compose(theory_source: str, link: str) -> str:
648:     """The model file for ``theory_source`` under the named link (links with a model-file form)."""
649:     if link not in LINKS:
650:         raise KeyError(f"no link {link!r}; the library has {sorted(LINKS)}")
651:     spec = LINKS[link].model_file
652:     if spec is None:
653:         raise ValueError(f"the {link!r} link has no model-file form; fit it with src.rsa_open.fit")
654:     tree = ast.parse(theory_source)
655:     functions = {n.name for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)}
656:     if LISTENER not in functions:
657:         raise ValueError(f"a theory must define {LISTENER}(params, ctx)")
658:     if "choice_probs" in functions:
659:         raise LinkClash("a theory may not define choice_probs: the link does")
660:     clash = sorted(set(_theory_params(tree)) & set(spec.params))
661:     if clash:
662:         raise LinkClash(f"theory parameter(s) {', '.join(clash)} belong to the {link!r} link")
663:     entries = ", ".join(f'"{k}": {v}' for k, v in spec.params.items())
664:     footer = (f"\n\n# --- link {link!r}, composed by src.rsa_open.links.compose "
665:               f"(docs/auto_open/PLAN.md §3) ---\n"
666:               f"{spec.imports}\n"
667:               f"PARAMS = {{**PARAMS, {entries}}}\n\n\n"
668:               f"{spec.body}")
669:     return theory_source.rstrip("\n") + footer
